architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: The uncertainty probe establishes whether a subsequent S1C41 performance-mitigation experiment can be executed and interpreted without unsupported stoichiometric or process-state assumptions.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Before any candidate performance result is inspected, obtain measured or supplier-supported functionality, equivalent-weight, moisture, and reactive-classification information for both AC1920 and TK100; calculate and document S1C41 reactive equivalents, NCO/OH index, MDI fraction, and complete mass balance without unverified substitutions; freeze all mixing, reaction, preheat, residence, loading, sampling, storage, age, and moisture conditions; require a contemporaneous matched E2 control and independently prepared realizations; and preregister numerical limits for acceptable 15-minute viscosity, repeat-to-repeat spread, delayed acceleration, nonmonotonicity, and temperature-shape failure. Only after every item is satisfied may S1C41 advance to a 120 °C, 15-90 minute hold test with measurements at least at 15, 60, and 90 minutes and a full 80-130 °C sweep unless state-calibration transferability is demonstrated.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the readiness probe and do not interpret a candidate performance test if any modifier property needed for reactive-equivalent accounting remains unknown, candidate-specific NCO/OH or mass balance requires an unsupported assumption, the matched E2 control or independent preparations are omitted, process history is not frozen, or any numerical operational and adjudication limit remains undefined when physical candidate measurements begin.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Pre-execution material and process characterization, followed conditionally by the matched 120 °C hold window from 15 through 90 minutes

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Preferred subsequent performance candidate because 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 cover both independently supported axes within the documented regions, but execution is deferred until modifier stoichiometry, moisture, process control, and prospective adjudication limits are resolved.

Lower total modifier burden, but 2.5 wt% TK100 is below the documented 3-10 wt% broad tackifier region and repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster; it is therefore a lower-dose uncertainty or robustness point, not the default full-mitigation experiment.
Provides interior-region coverage with 17.5 wt% acrylic and 5 wt% tackifier, but its 22.5 wt% total modifier burden is not justified before the lower-burden S1C41 can be interpreted.

Acrylic-only control with cleaner single-axis attribution, but it zeroes the independently supported tackifier axis and would be appropriate only if the intent were changed from performance mitigation to causal isolation.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The local experiments establish the failure mode: under the same 120 °C schedule, E5 had SI15-60 = 0.515 and SI15-90 = 0.931 versus 0.095 and 0.168 for E1, while E2 showed approximately 2.8-3.6-fold realization-level shifts. Paper-derived rheological rules from the audited local analysis indicate a shared temperature-response shape with realization-specific scale shifts inside the measured chemistry family, but they also require hold stability, initial viscosity, temperature response, and process state to be adjudicated separately. Curated PUR literature/database priors support an acrylic-like region around 15-25 wt% and a minor tackifier region broadly around 3-10 wt%, with repeated tackifier examples near 5 wt%; these priors guide the formulation family but do not predict the held-out local result or establish a molecular mechanism. Conservative experimental-design constraints introduce the matched E2 control, independent preparations, moisture and stoichiometry review, bounded 80-130 °C characterization, and prospectively frozen operational and repeatability limits. The Skeptic's objections are upheld: S1C40's 2.5 wt% tackifier dose is not adequately supported, minimum-burden reasoning was applied before sufficiency was established, and unresolved stoichiometry and process state prevent interpretation. The Robustness Adjudicator's conditional preference for S1C41 is accepted, but only as the subsequent performance candidate after uncertainty resolution. Immediate selection of S1C41 is withheld because unknown modifier reactivity and moisture could confound the formulation intervention with NCO/OH changes, and missing matched controls could confound it with realization state. Exact analogue distance is treated only as audit metadata. This decision therefore freezes an uncertainty probe rather than making an exact-property prediction.

evidence_coverage.note: S1C41 covers the acrylic-like lower supported region and the repeated approximately 5 wt% tackifier region; S1C40 does not robustly cover the tackifier region.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required first to obtain the canonical pre-validation assessment of formulation-only versus state-aware behavior, state-shift master-curve structure, one-point calibration value, temperature sensitivity, and the E1/E5 hold contrast before any candidate ranking.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the full measured low-drift reference trajectory and deterministic descriptors, rather than relying only on the supplied endpoint SI summary.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the full measured high-drift trajectory that defines the performance failure to be mitigated under the same local hold schedule.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Establish the measured reactive-core composition and transparent polyol, MDI, acrylic-like, tackifier-like, and combined-modifier fractions before interpreting candidate additions or checking stoichiometric feasibility.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After fixing the local hold-stability objective, obtain the auditable mapping from the E2 anchor to the independent acrylic and tackifier axes, candidate regions, and claim boundary needed to compare blinded candidates.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Check source-level evidence and limitations for the acrylic stability direction, including whether loading and modifier functionality are separable enough to support a bounded candidate region. These records remain directional and noncommensurate with the local 15-90 minute hold.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Verify the source-level basis for the minor tackifier range and its limitations before admitting a combined intervention; the approximately 5 wt% examples and below-about-10 wt% guidance are conservative search principles, not an optimum.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Absolute viscosity level at 120 °C at a predefined initial hold time, preserving the unknown source unit
Dimensionless hold drift SI15-60 and SI15-90, with lower absolute SI preferred
Shape and monotonicity of the complete 15-90 minute hold trajectory, including any acceleration or nonmonotonic behavior
Apparent temperature sensitivity over measured support rather than extrapolated temperatures
Run-to-run viscosity-level spread and whether one-point state calibration accounts for it
Distance from the E2 reactive-core anchor on acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes
Whether each active modifier axis has independent evidence support and remains within the pre-result bounds
Total combined-modifier fraction and resulting dilution or displacement of reactive-core components
NCO/OH index and uncertainty arising from modifier hydroxyl functionality, equivalent weights, and moisture
MDI fraction, polyol fraction, and mass-balance feasibility
Sensitivity to mixing, preheating, residence time, storage, retest delay, sampling, and moisture exposure
Evidence directness: local commensurate measurements versus directional external analogues versus conservative extrapolation controls
Information value if competing candidates have similar predicted performance but different uncertainty profiles
counterfactual_checks: If a candidate lowers the 15-minute viscosity but leaves SI15-60 or SI15-90 near the E5 trajectory, conclude that nominal viscosity was changed without mitigating the established failure.
If hold drift improves but the initial viscosity becomes unusable or temperature sensitivity becomes excessive within 80-130 °C, do not classify the candidate as an overall performance success.

If one-point state calibration collapses between-run offsets while preserving a common temperature-response curve, treat state calibration as necessary; if it does not, require fuller temperature characterization.
If independently prepared repeats differ by an amount comparable to E2's historical 2.8-3.6-fold spread, attribute low confidence to formulation ranking and prioritize process-state resolution.
If a combined acrylic-plus-tackifier candidate succeeds, do not infer synergy without single-axis controls; record only that the bounded combined intervention met the performance objective.
If a single-axis candidate performs as well as a combined candidate within repeatability uncertainty, prefer the simpler bounded intervention for lower extrapolation and attribution risk.
If acrylic loading changes hold behavior only when NCO/OH index also changes, test whether the apparent modifier effect is confounded by reactive stoichiometry.
If tackifier-containing candidates show instability or phase behavior, reconsider the external tackifier analogy rather than extrapolating from its documented melt-processability.
If the reactive-core-only candidate matches modifier-containing candidates on hold stability and viscosity after state calibration, reject the assumption that modifier addition is required.
If E1/E5 differences disappear under a harmonized process history, reinterpret the dominant issue as realization/process state rather than intrinsic formulation response.
planner.decision_goal: Select one blinded candidate experiment that prospectively mitigates the established 120 °C hot-hold viscosity drift while retaining usable viscosity within the measured 80-130 °C domain and controlling realization/process-state and stoichiometric uncertainty. The goal is not to infer an exact formulation optimum or recover the held-out formulation.
design_implications: Optimize hold stability as an independent response. A candidate that reaches an attractive viscosity at one time point but continues to rise strongly during the hold does not solve the observed failure.
Keep four decision dimensions separate: viscosity level, apparent temperature response, thermal-hold stability, and realization/process state.

Use 120 °C and the measured 15-90 minute window for the primary prospective hold comparison; do not translate literature results measured near 121 °C over 4-10 hours into an exact local acceptance threshold.

Treat E1 and E5 as directly commensurate local numeric hold anchors because they share the 120 °C schedule and SI definition. Treat external acrylic and tackifier findings as directional or analogue evidence, not directly commensurate local optima.

The repeated external acrylic examples near 15-25 wt% support a coarse acrylic-modifier region, while the 25 wt% low-OH versus higher-OH comparison directionally suggests that modifier functionality may matter. These findings do not establish the optimum loading or mechanism in the local system.

The external tackifier evidence supports a minor tackifier axis around 5 wt%, with below about 10 wt% used only as a conservative search bound. It does not prove that tackifier addition reduces local hold drift.

Because the intent is performance mitigation, a bounded acrylic-plus-tackifier intervention is admissible if each axis is independently supported, composition and stoichiometry remain feasible, and the candidate hypothesis confirms that the combination stays within the pre-result lattice. Single-axis selection is not mandatory unless causal attribution becomes the objective.
Candidate ranking must penalize extrapolation, uncertain modifier functionality, changes in NCO/OH balance, moisture sensitivity, and uncontrolled process history.

The E2 reactive core is the declared anchor. Modifier percentages must not be interpreted independently of how their addition changes total-formulation fractions, reactive equivalents, and MDI fraction.
No candidate order or identifier encodes rank or historical identity, and the candidate lattice supports only region/direction selection rather than exact recovery of a later formulation.
material_regularities_to_use: Within each measured run, viscosity decreased monotonically from 80 to 130 °C and was described well by an Andrade-type temperature relation, with reported run-level R2 values of 0.965-0.998.
Temperature response and realization state must be separated: smooth within-run temperature behavior coexists with large between-run viscosity-level shifts for E2.
The run-level apparent temperature-sensitivity slopes span approximately 4526-5358 K, so temperature sensitivity should be evaluated separately from absolute viscosity level.
Thermal-hold drift is formulation-dependent within the original measurements: E1 and E5 have sharply different 120 °C time trajectories over the same 15-90 minute support.
The supplied viscosity unit is unknown and must remain unknown; comparisons should preserve source values or use dimensionless descriptors such as SI.

The canonical state-aware summary is still required to confirm whether the observed run differences are adequately represented as state shifts on a shared master curve and whether one-point state calibration is justified.
planner.physical_failure_mode: The primary demonstrated failure is time-dependent viscosity rise during hot holding, not merely an unfavorable nominal viscosity. At 120 °C, E5 showed substantially greater drift than E1: SI15-60 was 0.515 versus 0.095 and SI15-90 was 0.931 versus 0.168. A separate realization/process-state risk is also present: E2 nominal temperature-sweep runs differed by roughly 2.8-3.6-fold across 80-130 °C, with descriptive CV values of about 0.46-0.58. Rheology alone does not identify the molecular cause of either behavior.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: A frozen 120 °C thermal-hold protocol with viscosity measured at least at 15, 60, and 90 minutes so SI15-60 and SI15-90 are directly comparable with E1 and E5.
The complete hold trajectory values, not only a final percentage change, to detect delayed or accelerating drift.
Initial 120 °C viscosity alongside hold drift so improved SI cannot conceal an unusable viscosity level.
A temperature sweep restricted to the measured 80-130 °C support, or the canonical one-point calibration protocol if the state-aware summary validates it for this use.

At least one independently prepared or independently realized repeat to separate formulation response from preparation/process state; repeatability statistics must remain descriptive when sample size is small.
Recorded batch age, storage history, retest delay, mixing order and intensity, preheat duration, thermal residence time, sampling time, and rheometer loading procedure.
Measured or supplier-supported hydroxyl functionality/equivalent information for modifiers, NCO/OH calculation, MDI fraction, and total mass balance.
Moisture control or measurement for reactive ingredients and the prepared batch.
Prospectively frozen acceptance criteria and any numerical objective weights before physical results are inspected.
uncertainty_triggers: Abstain or switch to uncertainty_resolution if the state-aware summary does not support transferable state calibration and only one realization can be measured.
Do not rank on nominal viscosity if candidate or reference run spread is comparable to the expected performance difference.
Escalate stoichiometric review if acrylic or tackifier hydroxyl functionality, equivalent weight, moisture content, or treatment as reactive versus nonreactive is unknown.
Reject as out of domain any decision requiring temperatures outside 80-130 °C or hold times outside 15-90 minutes unless a new protocol is explicitly justified.
Do not convert the external 15%, approximately 20%, or 25% acrylic examples into an exact local optimum; they are analogue-region anchors.
Do not convert the literature 25% increase over 4-10 hours into a local 15-90 minute pass/fail threshold.
Penalize or reject candidates exceeding the pre-result acrylic lattice bound of 30 wt% or the conservative tackifier bound of 10 wt%.
Reclassify the experiment as causal_isolation if the primary question becomes attribution to one modifier axis rather than mitigation of hold drift.
Treat unexpected nonmonotonicity, phase separation, gel formation, or inability to obtain a stable rheometer signal as feasibility or out-of-domain evidence rather than forced numeric performance.
Do not make a molecular-mechanism claim if the only supporting result is rheological.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate provides meaningful prospective mitigation of the established hot-hold viscosity-rise failure without relying on static viscosity as a proxy.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: On independently prepared realizations under the frozen protocol, both SI15-60 and SI15-90 must be below the respective midpoints between the directly commensurate E1 and E5 local anchors: SI15-60 < 0.305 and SI15-90 < 0.550. The complete trajectory must show no delayed acceleration or nonmonotonic instability, and the 15-minute viscosity must remain within an operational range frozen before results are inspected.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail if either SI threshold is not met, if the trajectory accelerates or becomes nonmonotonic, if phase separation, gel formation, or unstable rheometer response occurs, if initial viscosity is outside the prospectively frozen operational range, or if repeat-to-repeat spread is too large to distinguish candidate performance from realization-state variation.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Complete viscosity trajectory in the unknown source unit at 120 °C, measured at least at 15, 30, 60, and 90 minutes, with SI15-60 and SI15-90 calculated; also record the 15-minute viscosity and an 80-130 °C temperature response.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use the 15-minute viscosity at 120 °C as the realization-specific state anchor. Prepare at least one independent repeat under a frozen mixing, reaction, preheat, residence, loading, sampling, storage, age, and moisture protocol. Check whether the modified formulation follows the local shared 80-130 °C thermal-response shape within approximately the established 1.10 multiplicative calibration error; if not, do not apply one-point calibration and retain the full temperature sweep.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 minutes, with required measurements at 15, 60, and 90 minutes and a preferred intermediate point at 30 minutes

evidence_against: The 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the repeated external 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, so its sufficiency is a conservative low-dose hypothesis rather than a direct analogue anchor.
The 15 wt% acrylic anchor is directional and its literature fraction denominator is not verified as exact total-formulation wt%.
The modified chemistry lies outside the locally measured reactive-core-only family, so the local state-shift model must be validated rather than assumed transferable.
evidence_for: Covers both independently supported intervention axes: 15 wt% AC1920 and 2.5 wt% TK100 on the preserved E2 reactive-core proportions.
Directly interrogates the physical failure mode by testing a combined modifier intervention against the locally measured 120 °C time-dependent viscosity rise.

Local diagnosis supports changing formulation family because E1 and E5 showed sharply different hold trajectories, while requiring matched process-state control because realization shifts can dominate absolute viscosity.

External formulation knowledge supports the acrylic-like and tackifier-like directions; it does not predict the outcome. The 15 wt% acrylic level is directional lower-region evidence, while minor tackifier use is supported as a formulation family.
Within the strong-analogue, full-coverage candidate class, this is the minimum total modifier burden at 17.5 wt%, so it is the smallest justified departure from the characterized E2 chemistry.
key_uncertainty: Unknown modifier functionality and moisture may alter the true NCO/OH balance.
Missing mixing, reaction, preheat, residence, age, and sampling histories create high realization-state uncertainty.
Evidence supports a formulation region and intervention direction, not this exact composition as an optimum.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It is the lowest-burden candidate that still covers every independently supported performance axis. A matched 120 °C hold directly determines whether a small combined intervention mitigates drift rather than merely changing nominal viscosity. Failure would efficiently show that the minimum tackifier perturbation and/or lower acrylic boundary is insufficient.

evidence_against: Its 20 wt% total modifier burden is larger than S1C40 without local evidence that the additional tackifier is necessary.
External tackifier records establish compatibility and melt-processability, not reduced 120 °C hold drift.
The acrylic loading remains supported partly by directional, noncommensurate 15% evidence.
evidence_for: Covers both supported axes with 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 while preserving E2 core proportions.
The 5 wt% tackifier level lies within the directly reported 4.8-6.4 wt% external composition cluster, making this a stronger test of the minor-tackifier formulation family than S1C40.
It tests the same locally diagnosed hot-hold failure while increasing only the tackifier-like axis relative to S1C40, providing an interpretable robustness comparison if both can later be tested.
The candidate remains inside the conservative pre-result modifier bounds and strong analogue-support class.
key_uncertainty: Whether the stronger tackifier dose improves hold drift, only shifts viscosity level, or causes instability or phase behavior.
Unknown modifier reactivity and resulting NCO/OH balance.
Transferability of the local state-shift calibration to this modified formulation.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It tests whether placing the tackifier-like axis inside its repeated external composition cluster gives a more robust mitigation response. It is preferred over larger combined interventions because it retains the lowest acrylic boundary and avoids unnecessary modifier burden.

evidence_against: The 17.5 wt% acrylic level is an interpolation within a supported region, not an independently validated optimum.
The 2.5 wt% tackifier level remains below the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% external cluster.
No local resin-modified hold trajectory exists, and all process-history fields are missing.
evidence_for: Covers both supported axes with 17.5 wt% AC1920 and 2.5 wt% TK100 on the E2 core.
It remains within the externally supported 15-25 wt% acrylic family and tests a modest acrylic increase from S1C40 without dropping the tackifier axis.
The experiment directly measures the locally established failure mode and can distinguish inadequate lower-bound acrylic loading from a general failure of the combined intervention.
At 20 wt% total modifier, it is less burdensome than candidates using both approximately 20 wt% acrylic and 5 wt% tackifier.
key_uncertainty: Whether increasing acrylic loading changes hold drift independently of realization state.
Whether modifier functionality changes reactive stoichiometry.
Whether a modified formulation still follows the shared local temperature-response shape.
ranked_candidates.why_this_experiment_is_useful: It provides an interpretable nearby robustness point that increases the acrylic-like intervention while retaining full axis coverage. It is more informative for performance mitigation than an acrylic-only candidate, which would be a partial-coverage mechanistic control.

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: hot-hold drift is formulation-dependent under the same 120 °C schedule. E1 had SI15-60 = 0.095 and SI15-90 = 0.168, whereas E5 had SI15-60 = 0.515 and SI15-90 = 0.931.

Measured local evidence: viscosity decreased monotonically from 80 to 130 °C within each run, but E2 realization levels differed by approximately 2.8-3.6-fold; static viscosity therefore cannot be interpreted without process-state control.

Derived state-aware model rule: a shared thermal-response shape plus realization-specific viscosity-scale shift described the audited local family with R2 = 0.998, and one 120 °C anchor gave approximately 6-10% pooled multiplicative calibration error.

Derived design rule: thermal-hold stability, initial viscosity, temperature response, and realization state are separate decision coordinates; a static 120 °C viscosity value is not a proxy for hold stability.

External analogue evidence, directly commensurate only in composition percentage: acrylic-modified PUR examples repeatedly use approximately 19-20 wt% acrylic-like resin, and a separate comparison uses 25 wt%. Their viscosity and long-hold outcomes are not directly commensurate with the local 15-90 minute protocol.

External analogue evidence, directional/noncommensurate: 15% acrylic addition provides lower-region support, but its denominator is not verified as exact total-formulation wt%; the 121 °C, 4-8 hour acrylic stability comparisons support direction and functionality concern, not a local numeric threshold or mechanism.

External analogue evidence, directly commensurate only in composition percentage: tackifier-like PUR examples cluster around 4.8-6.4 wt%, with below approximately 10 wt% serving as conservative general guidance; these sources do not establish reduced local hold drift.

Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, compare candidates covering both independently supported modifier axes before partial-coverage controls, then prefer the minimum sufficient modifier burden within the scientifically supported family.

Unresolved uncertainty: AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality, equivalent weights, moisture, and treatment in the NCO/OH calculation are not supplied, and all candidates lack six major process-history fields.
proposer.scientific_target: Prospectively test whether a bounded acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like modification of the E2 reactive core mitigates the demonstrated 120 °C hot-hold viscosity rise over 15-90 minutes while preserving an operationally usable initial viscosity and controlling realization/process-state uncertainty.
unresolved_questions: What are the hydroxyl functionalities, equivalent weights, moisture contents, and reactive classifications of AC1920 and TK100?
What recalculated NCO/OH index results after accounting for modifier functionality and moisture?
What numerical initial-viscosity range is operationally usable? It must be frozen before candidate results are examined.
Will the state-shift master curve remain transferable after introducing both modifier axes?
Can matched E2 and, if feasible, E1/E5 references be realized under the same process history to separate formulation effects from laboratory-state effects?
Does S1C40's 2.5 wt% tackifier dose sufficiently engage the supported intervention axis, or is the approximately 5 wt% cluster represented by S1C41 required?
Evidence currently supports a bounded 15-20 wt% acrylic and minor-tackifier family for initial testing, not an exact composition or molecular mechanism.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Provides full region-supported coverage with 15 wt% AC1920 and 5 wt% TK100 at a modest 20 wt% total modifier burden; it is more evidentially robust than S1C40 but slightly more perturbative.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The experiment remains performance_mitigation and modifier stoichiometry and process controls are resolved.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Uses 17.5 wt% acrylic and 5 wt% tackifier, improving robustness to the uncertain 15 wt% acrylic denominator but increasing total modifier burden to 22.5 wt%.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: Greater weight is placed on interior acrylic-region support while retaining the 5 wt% tackifier cluster.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Its single 20 wt% acrylic axis gives cleaner attribution, but it does not test the full evidence-supported performance-mitigation strategy.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The intent is reclassified to causal_isolation of the acrylic-like axis.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Minimizes modifier burden, but failure would not distinguish an under-dosed tackifier axis from failure of the combined mitigation strategy.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: Independent pre-result evidence establishes 2.5 wt% TK100 as a sufficient tackifier intervention or the experiment is explicitly framed as a lower-dose uncertainty probe.

required_conditions: Verify AC1920 and TK100 functionality, equivalent weights, moisture contents, and reactive classifications.
Recalculate candidate-specific NCO/OH index, MDI fraction, reactive equivalents, and mass balance before formulation execution.
Use S1C41 rather than S1C40 for the subsequent performance test unless independent evidence supports 2.5 wt% TK100.
Include a contemporaneous matched E2 control under the same mixing, reaction, preheat, residence, loading, sampling, storage, age, and moisture conditions.
Use independently prepared realizations and freeze a quantitative repeat-to-repeat spread threshold that suspends formulation ranking.
Freeze a numerical operational range for the 15-minute viscosity before inspecting results.
Define quantitative criteria for delayed acceleration, nonmonotonicity, phase instability, and failure of the shared temperature-response shape.
Treat one-point state calibration as unvalidated for the modified chemistry unless transferability is demonstrated; otherwise use the full 80-130 °C sweep.
Label the SI midpoint criteria as conservative reconstructed decision thresholds and predefine how uncertainty in the single E1 and E5 trajectories will be handled.
Document outcome-blind candidate-grid and ranking provenance sufficiently to address the residual leakage concern.

robustness_checks.detail: The proposed 120 °C, 15-90 minute trajectory and SI15-60/SI15-90 measurements directly test the demonstrated time-dependent viscosity rise rather than relying on nominal viscosity.

The declared intent is performance_mitigation, so a dual-axis acrylic-like plus tackifier-like candidate is appropriate; single-axis candidates are mechanistic controls rather than default rank-1 choices.

S1C40 nominally activates both axes, but its 2.5 wt% TK100 is below the documented 3-10 wt% tackifier region and 4.8-6.4 wt% repeated cluster. It therefore does not robustly cover the independently supported tackifier intervention.

S1C40 was promoted over S1C41 primarily because of lower total modifier burden before sufficiency of the 2.5 wt% tackifier dose was established. Minimum burden is only a tie-break among sufficiently supported candidates.

Treating external evidence as regions rather than exact targets favors S1C41: 15 wt% acrylic is directional lower-region support and 5 wt% tackifier lies within the repeated minor-resin cluster. S1C40 loses support because 2.5 wt% tackifier is outside the stated broad region.

The general dual-axis strategy remains reasonable, but the exact S1C40 choice is unstable. Reasonable weighting of repeated tackifier examples reranks S1C41, while stronger weighting of the approximately 20 wt% acrylic examples could favor S1C46 or S1C51.

robustness_checks.check: Modifier burden versus stronger performance test
robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 provides the stronger supported dual-axis test at 20 wt% total modifier, only 2.5 percentage points above S1C40, without an unnecessarily large burden.

AC1920 and TK100 functionality, equivalent weights, moisture, reactive classifications, and candidate-specific NCO/OH index are unresolved. A performance result could therefore be confounded by altered reactive stoichiometry.

All candidates have high process-history uncertainty, and historical E2 viscosity varied approximately 2.8-3.6-fold. Independent repeats help, but a contemporaneous matched E2 control under the same process history is required for decisive interpretation.

The hold trajectory, SI endpoints, initial viscosity, and temperature response are appropriate. However, the operational initial-viscosity range, repeatability cutoff, delayed-acceleration rule, calibration-shape failure consequence, and uncertainty treatment for the single E1/E5 anchors remain unfrozen.
Rank 1 depends on the unsupported assumption that 2.5 wt% TK100 sufficiently engages the tackifier axis and on unresolved transferability of local state calibration to modified chemistry.
No held-out identity or outcome is supplied, but the exact fine grid and refinement algorithm were formalized after validation and lack a contemporaneous freeze artifact.

The Skeptic identified high-severity dose-support and stoichiometry problems plus inadequate matched process control. These are sufficient to reject immediate acceptance of S1C40 and require an uncertainty-resolution step before execution.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not adequately address the counterfactual that the supported tackifier intervention requires approximately 5 wt%; S1C41 directly tests that region, whereas S1C40 may only test an under-dosed axis.
The plan does not require a matched E2 control to test whether apparent improvement disappears under harmonized process history.
The plan does not specify how large repeat-to-repeat variation must be before formulation ranking is suspended.
The midpoint SI thresholds do not account for uncertainty from the single measured E1 and E5 hold trajectories.
If the modified formulation fails the shared temperature-shape check, the fallback full sweep is stated, but the acceptance consequences for overall performance are not prospectively defined.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate hypothesis defines the tackifier broad supported region as 3-10 wt% and the repeated cluster as 4.8-6.4 wt%. S1C40 contains only 2.5 wt% TK100. The proposer itself calls this a conservative low-dose hypothesis, yet the deterministic scorecard marks the tackifier axis covered and the proposal ranks S1C40 first.
critical_findings.issue: S1C40 is treated as a full-coverage performance candidate despite using an inadequately supported tackifier dose.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 is preferred because it is the minimum-burden member of the nominal strong-analogue/full-coverage class. No local modified-formulation hold data establish that 2.5 wt% tackifier sufficiently engages the independently supported axis. The supplied audit rules explicitly prohibit applying minimum sufficient intervention before sufficiency has been established.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 rationale improperly applies minimum sufficient intervention before intervention sufficiency is known.

critical_findings.evidence: AC1920 and TK100 hydroxyl functionality, equivalent weights, moisture, reactive classifications, and the resulting NCO/OH index are unknown. The original NCO/OH value of 1.8 applies only to the E2 reactive core, while every combined candidate dilutes that core and may add reactive equivalents.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometry is unresolved, making a formulation-performance result potentially confounded.

critical_findings.evidence: All candidates have six missing process-history fields and high process-history uncertainty. The plan requests an independent repeat and recorded controls but does not require a contemporaneous E2 or other matched reference under the same process history, despite historical E2 viscosity-level variation of approximately 2.8-3.6-fold.
critical_findings.issue: Process-state control is not sufficiently operationalized for a decisive comparison.

critical_findings.evidence: The operational 15-minute viscosity range is deferred to a later freeze, 'no delayed acceleration' has no numerical definition, and 'repeat-to-repeat spread is too large' has no predefined threshold. The SI midpoint thresholds are transparent interpolations between single E1 and E5 trajectories, but they are conservative decision rules rather than measured performance boundaries and lack uncertainty margins.
critical_findings.issue: Acceptance criteria remain partly unfrozen and statistically underdefined.

critical_findings.evidence: The state-aware tool limits the shared-shape model to the measured local chemistry family. S1C40 and S1C41 introduce two modifiers. The plan appropriately proposes checking transferability, but the approximately 1.10 error factor cannot be assumed as an established tolerance for these modified formulations.
critical_findings.issue: Transferability of one-point state calibration to the modified chemistry is unproven.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate-hypothesis output states that the current exact V2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. Although the payload states that held-out coordinates and outcomes were excluded, independent verification of outcome-blind fine-grid construction is unavailable.
critical_findings.issue: The candidate-grid provenance leaves a residual leakage concern.

interpretability_failures: A result cannot be cleanly assigned to modifier-family performance until modifier functionality, moisture, reactive classification, and recalculated NCO/OH index are documented.
Without a contemporaneous matched reference, preparation-state drift may be mistaken for formulation mitigation or failure.
Failure of S1C40 would not distinguish an insufficient 2.5 wt% tackifier perturbation from failure of the broader combined strategy.
The proposed repeatability failure rule is not quantitative, so an ambiguous result could be adjudicated post hoc.
The initial-viscosity usability range is not yet numerical, preventing a fully prospective overall-success decision.

leakage_check.detail: No held-out formulation identity or wet-lab result is visible in the supplied evidence, and the tools explicitly report outcome-blind use. However, the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment, with no contemporaneous freeze artifact available. This prevents a definitive pass.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly targets the measured 120 °C time-dependent viscosity rise, keeps static viscosity separate from hold stability, and includes state-aware measurements. However, rank-1 S1C40 is not adequately aligned with the evidence-supported tackifier region: its 2.5 wt% TK100 is below the stated 3-10 wt% broad region and the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. Calling it full evidence coverage and then invoking minimum modifier burden applies minimum-sufficient-intervention reasoning before sufficiency has been established.

required_corrections: Resolve AC1920 and TK100 functionality, equivalent weights, moisture, reactive classification, mass balance, and candidate-specific NCO/OH index before executing or interpreting a performance experiment.
Do not classify S1C40 as full evidence-supported coverage unless independent pre-result evidence supporting 2.5 wt% TK100 is supplied.

After stoichiometric review, rerank S1C41 above S1C40 because S1C41 covers both intervention axes within the documented evidence regions; retain S1C40 only as a lower-dose uncertainty or robustness point.

Require a contemporaneous matched E2 reference, or another explicitly justified state/process control, under the same mixing, preheat, residence, loading, age, storage, sampling, and moisture conditions.
Freeze a numerical operational range for 15-minute viscosity before results are inspected.
Define quantitative criteria for delayed acceleration, nonmonotonicity, calibration-shape failure, and unacceptable repeat-to-repeat spread.

Label the SI midpoint thresholds explicitly as reconstructed conservative decision thresholds derived from local anchors, not as measured physical boundaries, and specify how uncertainty in the single E1 and E5 trajectories will be handled.
Document the provenance of the fine candidate grid and ranking rule sufficiently to demonstrate that S1C40 and S1C41 were not selected using held-out formulation identity or outcome.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally avoids claiming an exact optimum, local molecular mechanism, tackifier causality, or direct commensurability of long-duration literature holds. Its main boundary error is evidentiary classification of the 2.5 wt% tackifier dose, not an explicit mechanistic claim.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: Check source-level evidence and limitations for the acrylic stability direction, including whether loading and modifier functionality are separable enough to support a bounded candidate region. These records remain directional and noncommensurate with the local 15-90 minute hold.

result.agent_hint: A 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer formulation showed substantially slower viscosity rise than the equal-loading higher-OH acrylic comparator; this supports both a 25% acrylic candidate level and the hypothesis that lower reactive-group density can improve hot-hold stability.
result.limitation: Different acrylic chemistry and much longer hold window; does not establish the local mechanism.
result.pattern: PPG1000 + PPG2000 + polyester polyol + low-OH acrylic copolymer + MDI

result.agent_hint: At the same 25 wt% acrylic loading, the higher-OH acrylic analogue exhibited roughly twice the reported 8 h viscosity increase of the low-OH example, making modifier functionality a plausible stability variable rather than loading alone.
result.limitation: Patent comparison; acrylic materials are not AC1920 and the result is not a direct local-system measurement.
result.pattern: same formulation as Example 10 but higher-OH acrylic copolymer

result.agent_hint: A functional-tackifier-containing formulation had lower reported stability rise than the no-acrylic/no-functional-tackifier comparator in the same example set, supporting the idea that modifier identity can change hot-melt stability.
result.limitation: Other formulation variables including MDI differ; not an isolated causal comparison.
result.pattern: PPG2025 + PPG4025 + polyester polyol + functional tackifier + MDI

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: Verify the source-level basis for the minor tackifier range and its limitations before admitting a combined intervention; the approximately 5 wt% examples and below-about-10 wt% guidance are conservative search principles, not an optimum.

result.agent_hint: Tackifying-resin-modified PUR is an externally documented formulation family; do not restrict the search to fully reactive polyol/isocyanate mixtures.
result.limitation: Single patent example; does not report thermal-hold drift.
result.pattern: polyester polyol + PPG425 + tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Hydrocarbon resin can coexist with reactive PUR while retaining measurable melt-processability; include a minor tackifier/hydrocarbon-resin axis rather than fixing the modifier at zero.
result.limitation: Different polyols and application; no thermal-hold stability trajectory.
result.pattern: multiple polyester polyols + PPG425 + hydrocarbon resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Acrylic-tackifying-resin-modified PUR around 20% of the total formulation is externally documented; 20% is therefore a defensible coarse candidate level, not a value inferred from the local follow-up result.
result.limitation: Different molecular weights, catalysts and application; viscosity is a single-temperature observation, not a hold-stability measurement.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: Repeated examples independently anchor an acrylic-resin design level near 20% while preserving melt processability.
result.limitation: Different chemistry and process history; no causal stability proof.
result.pattern: polyoxypropylene diol + polyester diols + acrylic tackifying resin + MDI

result.agent_hint: The external database supports an acrylic-modified formulation family and provides a reproducible anchor around 20% for coarse candidate generation.
result.limitation: External analogue only; not evidence for the current formulation's exact optimum.
